_comment: AOT images of what the app's users run most: Java and Maven (libjvm.so), Kimi Code (node),
Claude Code (claude.exe, Bun) and musl under all of them, and what their sessions run most:
bash and python3 (their workloads 2.3 and 4.2 times faster with the images); git and gh, which
Claude Code's sessions run often: their workloads were no faster with images, but with the
built-in JIT their code went into its code region, more of it than any other program's, where an
image keeps it out (guest/app/git_train.sh, guest/app/gh_train.sh). Recorded by
record_app_images.sh on the root the app ships, with the
packages below at the versions apk and npm give that day: an image serves the module it was
recorded from (its ELF build-id), so record again after the app's root or those packages
change (Claude Code updates itself often). node is recorded in both the modes the app runs it
in with its image (guest/kimi/kimi_image.sh): the interpreter, the JIT not translating, and V8's
tiers, the JIT translating with room in its code region, where V8's compilers run too (kernel/
exec.c). claude.exe is recorded with
JavaScriptCore's JIT off, as the app's claude-wrapper runs it, in print mode, a session of
tools and a long session on its interactive screen (guest/claude/claude_image.sh): the app
runs it with no executable memory, where a block the image lacks runs through the gadgets.
busybox (the root's commands:
ls, grep, sed, find and the rest of what a session runs), ssh (git over ssh) and libcrypto (ssh's
and TLS's) came in 2026-11-24; ssh's and libcrypto's workloads talk to an sshd in an ish of its
own, on a root of its own (sshd: its packages, and the images that need it).
